questions.q: What does the `source` field of an ArgoCD `Application` describe?
options: The Kubernetes cluster and namespace the manifests get applied to
The Lua script used for a custom health check
Where the desired manifests come from — the Git repo, revision, and path
The list of users allowed to trigger a manual sync
questions.explain: source names the Git repoURL, targetRevision (branch/tag/commit), and path (often a Kustomize overlay) that the Application treats as its desired state.

questions.q: An ArgoCD Application shows Sync status 'Synced' and Health status 'Degraded'. What does that combination mean?
options: The correct manifests from Git were applied, but the running workload itself is failing
Git and the live cluster disagree, and nothing is actually running yet
ArgoCD has not finished computing either status yet
The Application was deleted but prune has not run
questions.explain: Sync status and Health status are independent dimensions. Synced means the live state matches Git; Degraded means the workload that was applied is failing on its own terms (bad image, crash loop, failed probe).

questions.q: Which values does ArgoCD's Sync status actually use?
options: Healthy and Degraded
Running and Stopped
Synced and OutOfSync
Succeeded and Failed
questions.explain: Sync status only answers whether the live cluster state matches the desired state in Git: Synced or OutOfSync. Healthy/Degraded belong to the separate Health status dimension.

questions.q: What does setting `syncPolicy.automated.selfHeal: true` change about ArgoCD's behavior?
options: It deletes resources from the cluster that were removed from Git
It reverts a manually edited live resource back to match Git on the next reconciliation, instead of just flagging the drift
It disables health checks for that Application entirely
It requires a human to approve every sync before it applies
questions.explain: selfHeal makes ArgoCD actively correct drift caused by direct edits to live resources, reapplying the Git-defined state rather than leaving it flagged as OutOfSync.

questions.q: Without `syncPolicy.automated`, how does an ArgoCD Application behave when Git changes?
options: It immediately and silently applies the new manifests with no record of the change
It refuses to ever detect drift
It applies changes only during a scheduled maintenance window
It computes and displays OutOfSync, but a human has to trigger the actual sync
questions.explain: With no automated block, ArgoCD defaults to manual sync: it will show OutOfSync once it detects a difference, but won't apply anything until a human runs argocd app sync or clicks Sync in the UI.
